nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free.tree:
- Machine Learning — Teaching computers to learn patterns from data.
  - Foundations — Core mathematical and probabilistic concepts needed for ML.
    - Vector Dot Product — Computes the sum of element‑wise products of two vectors.
    - Matrix Multiplication — Produces a matrix by combining rows of the first with columns of the second.
    - Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors — Values and vectors that reveal a matrix’s intrinsic scaling directions.
    - Bayes' Theorem — Updates probability of a hypothesis given new evidence using prior knowledge.
  - Data Preparation — Techniques to clean, transform, and prepare data for modeling.
    - Handling Missing Values — Strategies to impute or remove absent data points in a dataset.
    - Feature Scaling — Rescales features to a common range, improving algorithm convergence.
    - One-Hot Encoding — Converts categorical variables into binary columns for model consumption.
    - Principal Component Analysis (PCA) — Reduces dimensionality by projecting data onto orthogonal variance‑maximizing axes.
  - Supervised Learning — Learning a mapping from input features to known output labels.
    - Linear Regression — Fits a straight line to predict continuous outcomes from features.
    - Logistic Regression — Models class probabilities using a sigmoid function on linear scores.
    - Decision Tree — Splits data recursively by feature thresholds to form a predictive tree.
    - Random Forest — Aggregates many decision trees to reduce variance and improve accuracy.
    - Support Vector Machine — Finds the optimal hyperplane that maximally separates classes.
    - Feedforward Neural Network — Layers of neurons process data forward to learn complex patterns.
  - Unsupervised Learning — Discovering hidden patterns in data without explicit labels.
    - k-Means Clustering — Partitions data into k clusters by minimizing intra‑cluster variance.
    - Hierarchical Clustering — Builds a tree of clusters by iteratively merging or splitting groups.
    - DBSCAN — Groups dense regions and marks outliers as noise based on density.
    - Gaussian Mixture Model — Models data as a blend of multiple Gaussian distributions.
  - Model Evaluation — Methods to assess model performance and generalization ability.
    - k-Fold Cross-Validation — Splits data into k folds, training on k‑1 and validating on the remaining.
    - Precision and Recall — Precision measures exactness; recall measures completeness of positive predictions.
    - ROC AUC — Quantifies a classifier’s ability to rank positives higher than negatives.
    - Bias-Variance Tradeoff — Describes the tension between model simplicity and sensitivity to data.
  - Advanced Topics — Advanced techniques that extend and deploy machine learning models.
    - Bagging — Trains models in parallel on bootstrap samples and averages their predictions.
    - Boosting — Sequentially trains models, each correcting errors of its predecessor.
    - Stacking — Combines multiple model predictions using a meta‑learner for improved performance.
    - Model Deployment — Exports a trained model to a serving environment for real‑time inference.

- Deep Learning — Deep learning teaches multi-layer neural networks to learn complex patterns.
  - Foundations of Neural Networks — Covers basic neurons, activations, and loss functions.
    - Perceptron — A single-layer neural network that makes linear predictions.
    - Sigmoid Activation — Smooth S-shaped function mapping inputs to values between 0 and 1.
    - ReLU Activation — Rectified linear unit outputting zero for negative inputs, else input.
    - Binary Cross-Entropy Loss — Loss measuring performance of classification models with two output classes.
  - Core Architectures — Introduces key network structures like feedforward, CNN, and RNN blocks.
    - Feedforward Neural Network — Network where information moves forward from input to output layers.
    - Convolutional Layer — Applies filters to extract spatial features from input data.
    - Pooling Layer — Reduces spatial dimensions while retaining important features.
    - Residual Block — Allows gradients to bypass layers via skip connections to ease training.
  - Training Techniques — Describes optimization, regularization, and learning rate schedules.
    - Stochastic Gradient Descent — Updates parameters using gradient computed on a random data subset.
    - Adam Optimizer — Adaptive learning rate method combining momentum and RMSprop benefits.
    - Dropout — Randomly disables neurons during training to prevent overfitting.
    - Step Decay Learning Rate — Reduces learning rate by a factor after fixed epochs.
  - Advanced Models — Explores modern architectures such as Transformers, GANs, and self‑supervised methods.
    - Transformer Encoder — Stack of self-attention and feedforward layers processing sequences.
    - Generative Adversarial Network — Two networks, generator and discriminator, trained adversarially to create data.
    - Variational Autoencoder — Encodes data to a distribution, then decodes to generate new samples.
    - Contrastive Learning — Learns representations by pulling similar samples together and pushing dissimilar apart.
  - Deployment & Practices — Covers model optimization, transfer learning, and deployment best practices.
    - Model Pruning — Removes unnecessary weights or neurons to shrink model size.
    - Quantization — Represents weights with lower-bit numbers to accelerate inference.
    - Transfer Learning — Reuses knowledge from a pre-trained model on a new task.
    - Fine-tuning Pre-trained Models — Adjusts a pre-trained model's weights for a specific downstream task.

- Natural Language Processing — Study how computers understand and generate human language.
  - Text Preprocessing — Clean and split raw text into tokens for further processing.
    - Tokenization — Splitting text into words, subwords, or characters as discrete units.
    - Text Normalization — Transforming text to a standard form (lowercase, removing punctuation).
    - Stop-Word Removal — Eliminating common words that add little meaning to the text.
  - Feature Extraction — Convert text into numerical features that models can learn from.
    - Bag-of-Words — Representing text as unordered counts of vocabulary terms.
    - TF-IDF — Weighting term frequency by inverse document frequency to highlight important words.
    - N‑gram Language Model — Predicting the next word based on the previous n‑1 word sequence.
    - Word2Vec — Learning dense vector representations of words from their contextual usage.
    - BERT Embeddings — Contextual word embeddings generated by bidirectional transformer encoders.
  - Core NLP Tasks — Fundamental linguistic tasks that extract structure and meaning from text.
    - Part-of-Speech Tagging — Assigning grammatical categories (noun, verb, etc.) to each token.
    - Named Entity Recognition — Identifying and classifying proper nouns like persons, organizations, locations.
    - Dependency Parsing — Determining grammatical relationships between words in a sentence.
    - Semantic Role Labeling — Labeling the predicate‑argument structure of a sentence.
    - Sentiment Analysis — Determining whether text expresses positive, negative, or neutral emotion.
  - Sequence Modelling — Models that capture sequential dependencies in text data.
    - Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) — Neural networks that process sequences by maintaining a hidden state over time.
    - Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) — A gated RNN variant that mitigates vanishing gradients with memory cells.
    - Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) — A simpler gated RNN that uses update and reset gates for sequence modeling.
    - Attention Mechanism — Weighting input elements dynamically to focus on relevant parts for prediction.
    - Transformer Architecture — Stacked self‑attention layers enabling parallel processing of sequences.
  - Applications and Evaluation — Real‑world NLP applications and how their performance is measured.
    - Machine Translation — Automatically converting text from one language to another.
    - Question Answering — Producing concise answers to natural language questions from a context.
    - Text Summarization — Creating a short summary that preserves the key information of a document.
    - Dialogue Systems — Building agents that can engage in coherent multi‑turn conversations.
    - BLEU Score — Metric measuring n‑gram overlap between machine and reference translations.
    - ROUGE Score — Metric evaluating summary quality by overlapping n‑grams and sequences.
    - Perplexity — Measure of how well a probability model predicts a sample; lower is better.

- Reinforcement Learning — Study of agents learning optimal behavior through interaction with an environment.
  - Foundations — Core concepts underlying sequential decision making in RL.
    - Markov Decision Process — Mathematical framework for modeling decision making where outcomes are partly random.
    - Bellman Equation — Recursive relation linking value of a state to values of successor states.
    - Value Iteration — Iterative algorithm that computes optimal value function by Bellman backups.
    - Policy Iteration — Alternates between policy evaluation and improvement to find optimal policy.
  - Value-Based Methods — Methods that learn value functions to derive optimal policies.
    - Q-Learning — Off‑policy TD learning that updates Q‑values using the max next‑state value.
    - SARSA — On‑policy TD learning that updates Q‑values using the actual next action.
    - Deep Q-Network — Uses deep neural networks to approximate Q‑values for high‑dimensional states.
    - Double Q-Learning — Reduces overestimation bias by decoupling action selection from value evaluation.
    - Dueling Network Architecture — Splits network into value and advantage streams for better Q‑value estimation.
  - Policy Gradient Methods — Directly optimize policies using gradient ascent on expected returns.
    - REINFORCE — Monte‑ Carlo policy gradient method that updates policies using episode returns.
    - Actor-Critic — Combines value‑function critic with policy‑gradient actor to reduce variance.
    - Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C) — Uses advantage function to stabilize and improve policy gradient updates.
    - Trust Region Policy Optimization — Constrains policy updates to a trust region for stable monotonic improvement.
    - Proximal Policy Optimization — Clips objective to limit policy changes, enabling robust and scalable training.
  - Model-Based & Planning — Learn environment models to plan and improve sample efficiency.
    - Dyna-Q — Combines Q‑learning with planning using a learned model of the environment.
    - Monte Carlo Tree Search — Builds a search tree using random simulations to estimate action values.
    - Probabilistic Dynamics Models — Learns distributions over next states to capture uncertainty in predictions.
    - Model-Based Policy Optimization — Iteratively learns a model and optimizes policy via back‑propagation through planning.
  - Exploration & Advanced Topics — Strategies and extensions for effective exploration and complex RL scenarios.
    - Epsilon-Greedy — Chooses random actions with probability ε, otherwise the greedy action.
    - Upper Confidence Bound — Selects actions balancing estimated value and uncertainty via confidence intervals.
    - Thompson Sampling — Samples action values from posterior distributions to balance exploration and exploitation.
    - Curiosity-Driven Exploration — Uses intrinsic motivation based on prediction error to encourage novel state visits.
    - Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning — Studies learning dynamics when multiple agents interact in shared environments.
    - Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning — Decomposes tasks into higher‑level goals and lower‑level policies for efficiency.
    - Safe Reinforcement Learning — Ensures agents satisfy constraints while learning optimal policies in uncertain environments.
    - Offline Reinforcement Learning — Learns policies from fixed datasets without further environment interaction.
